thread:
ana: FYI opened a docs PR that rearranges the Optimize toolkit page to surface Node + Python quick recipes first. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/802

ryan: awesome. can we include a small runnable Node snippet demonstrating route-level batching + KV prefix caching? many infra folks want a QS example for productionizing.

tess: yes please. suggest the Node snippet live in /sdk/node/recipes.md and link from /guides/optimize. keep it 6 lines max. also add a one-line note about monitoring token cost after enabling batching.

ana: (typo: this should be @ana) here's a draft Node snippet i tried: 

```js
const { RedwoodClient } = require('@redwood/inference');
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
// apply a latency-first batching profile to a route and enable KV prefix caching
await client.optimize.applyBatchingProfile({ route: '/chat', profile: 'latency-first' });
await client.optimize.enableCaching({ route: '/chat', mode: 'kv-prefix' });
```

ryan: nice. minor API naming question: we usually use camelCase in Node but guarantee parity with Python. `enableCaching` vs `configureCaching`? whichever matches SDK. mark can confirm.

mark: Prefer `configureCaching` in the Node SDK, to mirror server-side config verbs. also add a short fallback note: if 'kv-prefix' is unsupported on model variant, the platform will fall back to 'none' and emit a warning event.

ana: added that fallback sentence in the guide. also moved the big quant-profiles table into an appendix and added an anchor: #quantization-profiles so linkcheck stops failing.

docs-bot: CI for PR #802 1/03 linkcheck: previously failing anchor fixed. style/lint: one warning (code fence language missing for node snippet).

tess: i'll add the language tag for the fenced code and a one-liner under the snippet mentioning when to prefer full response caching (small stable responses) vs KV prefix (longer contexts with high prefix reuse).

ryan: can we add a tiny migration checklist for Node in the guide? like: 1) find heavy routes 2) try low-latency profile 3) run perf eval 4) stage on dedicated pool. one sentence each.

ana: added a short Node checklist near the top. also included a sample curl command for the monitoring endpoint: 

```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/monitoring/route-usage?route=/chat
```

mark: LGTM after code fence fix. can one of you do a quick smoke test of the snippet locally? if green i'll approve.

tess: smoke-tested the Node snippet but had to tweak the import path in our monorepo. left a note in the PR comments.

ana: great, i'll squash and request reviews from @mark and @ryan. target merge tomorrow morning to sync with a partner demo. :rocket:
